prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT=Target Off Block Time: issued only if capacity/ground path allow; frozen at horizon unless exception recorded; revised only on turnaround-actor confirmation. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode; Capacity Reduction State (Airport Duty Manager may declare localized); both allow binding metering; Recovery Phase; Contingency Fallback State (Contingency Operations Console). Elements: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time; evaluates swaps); Departure Metering Service (Emberline; recalculates advisories post-swap, prevents departure-fix peaks); North/South Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter; East/West Apron Sensors; Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; swap entry; validates via Identity Access Service; pending if customs incomplete, blocking SAE publication); Collaborative Decision Log (flights, reason code, confirmations, governance outcome, decision time); Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf); Gate Conflict Detector; Airline Interface Adapter; Handling Resource Planner; Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern; MUST meet latency); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; MUST refresh within 5 s); Common Situation Display (shows updated CTT/TOBT); Audit Event Ledger (approvals, rejections, cancellations, overrides, releases); Business Rules Registry; Sector Load Monitor; Flight Data Exchange (publishes Flight Intent Message only after swap final and time-synced); Performance Analytics Warehouse; Time Synchronization Service; Arrival Regulation Console (Nightjar); Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard). Swap governance: Slot Coordinator reviews SAE exceptions, sends Slot Swap Permission Email only after checks recorded; Aircraft Operator Representatives record concurrence in Portal; Network Operations Liaison monitors aggregate displacement; Regional Flow Manager may suspend substitution in Capacity Reduction State, resolves disputes; Tower Supervisor may reject swaps; Ramp Control Lead checks stands/pushback/tugs; Airport Duty Manager uses Apron Sweep Completion Note; Airline Operations Coordinator uses customs release note; customs release prerequisite for moving international departure earlier.

New part:
S688: The System Support Engineer investigates technical failures in submission, validation, or publication without altering the operational decision unless authorized through the defined control process.
S689: The Post Operations Report includes swap volume, rejection reasons, approval latency, compliance with revised times, and any equity concerns identified during the operating period.
S690: Aerodrome infrastructure events are treated as capacity inputs when they affect runway availability, taxi route usability, stand access, lighting performance, or supporting navigation services.
S691: The Regional Flow Platform records each event as an operational constraint with an effective time, expected duration, affected resource, confidence level, and approving authority.
S692: The Airport Duty Manager is responsible for ensuring that declared service reductions are entered promptly and that the operational description is consistent with local aerodrome control procedures.
S693: The Tower Supervisor uses the Runway Lighting Outage Card to confirm which runway lighting elements are unavailable before approving the operational status shown in the Tower Sequence Manager.
S694: When lighting performance limits night or low-visibility operations, the Capacity Assessment Module converts the limit into a runway configuration constraint rather than treating it as a general advisory.
S695: The Airport CDM Portal presents infrastructure events to authorized airport, airline, and flow management users as part of the shared operating picture.
S696: The Regional Flow Manager reviews the published constraint when it changes the usable runway rate, taxi-out predictability, or the feasibility of the active demand plan.
S697: The Capacity Assessment Module calculates the operational effect by comparing the affected resource with the current Airport Capacity Plan and the active weather state.
S698: If the event reduces arrival throughput, the Arrival Regulation Console applies the revised Airport Acceptance Rate after confirmation by the Regional Flow Manager.
S699: If the event reduces departure throughput, the Departure Metering Service updates metering rates and provides revised inputs to the Slot Allocation Engine.
S700: The Slot Allocation Engine uses the reduced capacity value to protect fairness while avoiding schedules that exceed the declared infrastructure capability.
S701: The Demand Prediction Service recalculates short-term demand against the constrained capacity so that delay and queue forecasts reflect the published limitation.
S702: The Tower Sequence Manager displays the accepted constraint to support runway sequencing decisions and to reduce conflicting tactical instructions.
S703: The Ramp Movement Board receives the same operational status so that apron movements can be coordinated with restricted taxi routes or stand access limitations.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
